--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Prisma client creates new connections in production
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L20)
Evidence: Code instantiates new PrismaClient unconditionally in production and only caches it on globalThis when NODE_ENV !== "production" (pattern: new PrismaClient(...) without global cache for production).
Impact: On serverless Next deployments this creates fresh DB connections per cold start and will exhaust Postgres connection limits under moderate concurrency (~tens of concurrent functions), causing connection pool exhaustion and 5xx failures.
Fix: Always cache the PrismaClient on globalThis in all envs (or use a managed pooler like PgBouncer and set pooling configs).

[DB-2] Product detail loads all reviews (unbounded) per request
File: src/app/api/products/[slug]/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: prisma.product.findUnique({ where:{slug}, include: { reviews: true, ... } }) — pulls the entire reviews array and then computes average in application code.
Impact: For popular products with many reviews this will blow up memory/CPU and cause high query latency and DB IOPS at scale (CRITICAL for product pages under 10x QPS).
Fix: Do not include full reviews; fetch aggregated counts/avg via Prisma aggregate/count or paginate reviews (cursor/limit) and calculate summaries in the DB.

finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Prisma client creates new connections in production
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L20)
Evidence: Code instantiates new PrismaClient unconditionally in production and only caches it on globalThis when NODE_ENV !== "production" (pattern: new PrismaClient(...) without global cache for production).
Impact: On serverless Next deployments this creates fresh DB connections per cold start and will exhaust Postgres connection limits under moderate concurrency (~tens of concurrent functions), causing connection pool exhaustion and 5xx failures.
Fix: Always cache the PrismaClient on globalThis in all envs (or use a managed pooler like PgBouncer and set pooling configs).

[DB-2] Product detail loads all reviews (unbounded) per request
File: src/app/api/products/[slug]/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: prisma.product.findUnique({ where:{slug}, include: { reviews: true, ... } }) — pulls the entire reviews array and then computes average in application code.
Impact: For popular products with many reviews this will blow up memory/CPU and cause high query latency and DB IOPS at scale (CRITICAL for product pages under 10x QPS).
Fix: Do not include full reviews; fetch aggregated counts/avg via Prisma aggregate/count or paginate reviews (cursor/limit) and calculate summaries in the DB.

[DB-3] Order update flow and coupon decrement are not atomic
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts (L1-L220, L220-L540)
Evidence: Coupon find + update is performed separately before order creation, and the "existingOrder" branch updates order and then runs multiple create/update/delete orderItem calls in JS loops without enclosing them in a single transaction.
Impact: Financial data inconsistency and double-spend risk: at moderate concurrency, coupon quantity or order_items can be partially applied (or decremented) leading to incorrect inventory/coupon counts or orphaned state.
Fix: Wrap coupon decrement + order create/update + all order_item upserts/deletes in a single DB transaction ($transaction) and use DB constraints/affected-rows checks to ensure idempotency.

[DB-4] Stock decrement in payment verification is a write hotspot
File: src/app/api/checkout/verify-payment/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: Inside a prisma.$transaction the code loops over order.orderItems and executes sequential tx.productColor.update / tx.product.update to decrement stock per item.
Impact: Concurrent confirmations for the same SKU will serialize and produce row-level lock contention, increasing latency and eventually blocking checkouts under concurrent buyers for the same product (breaks at dozens of concurrent hits on hot SKUs).
Fix: Shorten lock duration and batch updates (single UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (...) with stock checks / use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE once), or use optimistic locking/compare-and-swap and reattempt, and validate rowsAffected for stock underflow.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-5] Products listing returns all products with relations (no pagination)
File: src/app/api/products/route.ts (L1-L160)
Evidence: prisma.product.findMany({ include: { colors: ... }, orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' } }) with no take/skip/cursor, returning full rows and related colors for every product.
Impact: As products grow, this will increase DB CPU, memory and response times and cause large network payloads; at higher QPS this will degrade latency and increase DB IOPS.
Fix: Add cursor/limit pagination (take/skip or cursor-based), and only select required fields and a small relation subset.

[DB-6] Missing index for high-select/order columns (createdAt)
File: prisma/schema.prisma (Product model) (L1-L140)
Evidence: Product is ordered by createdAt in product listing, but schema has no index on createdAt (no @@index on that column).
Impact: ORDER BY on createdAt over a large products table will force sorts and increase DB CPU and latency as rows grow (painful at tens of thousands+ rows).
Fix: Add an index on createdAt (or composite indexes tailored to the common queries) or use a paginated query that leverages an indexed cursor.

--- INFO ---

[DB-7] Database and ORM
File: prisma/schema.prisma
Evidence: Prisma + PostgreSQL are used (datasource provider = "postgresql"), so connection pooling and row-level locking semantics apply.
